claim_ceiling: ONE_BOUNDED_THREE_LEVEL_EXECUTION_COMPOSITION != GENERAL_RECURSIVE_HIERARCHY != THREE_LEVEL_END_TO_END_LEARNING. Both controllers are already trained/qualified two-level controllers, and the harness supplies an opaque mapping from the L2 request token to an L1 current context. The middle controller independently chooses the L0 request. Cross-level learning/currentness propagation after internal middle drift is not established here.

harness_scar.repair: assert lawful MIDDLE_ABSTAIN rather than MIDDLE_NO_CURRENT_PROPOSAL; no production/mechanism change

observed: Flattened two-level control and nested three-level execution both produced the same top request choices and +2 top observable consequence for the two learned query classes.

Inside each top request handler the middle Microseed independently ran current_proposal, nominated its own bounded action intent, and executed its own bound L0 request; L2 never supplied the leaf request token.

Top handler receipt hid leaf target/local mean; leaf details existed only in a separate red-team log. Top and middle maintained separate capability-registry contract objects even where content-addressed IDs coincided.
No hierarchy_manager, parent_manager, or desired_state_registry emerged in either controller.

When the required middle leaf target was REFUSED, the middle controller produced a proposal but ABSTAINED at its own bounded-intent gate; no leaf world receipt occurred while the top request itself remained an ordinary emitted request.
oarr: Flattened direct two-level handler is observationally equivalent at the top boundary; therefore the nested level does not by itself justify a new recursive hierarchy mechanism.
